panel.says: one row per entity per period: every ("avalanche.id", "date") pair in this table is unique, so rowCount (1406) counts readings, never subjects — there are 1406 of those
panel.decidedBy: every ("avalanche.id", "date") pair is unique across all 1406 rows, and "avalanche.id" holds no blank

coverage.says: a period's own step being present is not the same as every entity being present in it: the fullest period here carries 17 entities and the thinnest carries 1

aggregates.says: an aggregate here is a row of this table that is the SUM of other rows of the same table. byArithmetic is DECIDED from the numbers: the same set of rows adds up to it in every period. byStructure is a proposal and nothing more — a row whose code is shaped unlike the rest of the column, or missing from it — and it also sweeps in places whose code is merely unusual. Take a proposal as a question to put to the journalist, never as an answer.

arithmetic.reason: the structural test set no row of this table apart, so there was no candidate to put to the arithmetic — a set of rows that happens to add up to another is a coincidence until something else says that row is different

structure.reason: no column of this table holds one stable code per entity with a shape most of them share

periodNotASequence.says: "date" was read as the period from its NAME, and this profiler's own typing does not make it a sequence — its gaps are null, so nothing here can say which steps it skips

header.says: this file's header is on line 4; the 3 lines above it are a publisher's banner and are not data
banner: WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF
Fatal avalanche accidents in Switzerland since 1936-1937

statedIncompleteness.says: the frozen prose states no incompleteness in English and French; a dataset that states one in another language is not read here
